ALBANY, NEW YORK

May 8, 1995

3:04 p.m.

REGULAR SESSION SENATOR JOHN A. DeFRANCISCO, Acting President STEPHEN F. SLOAN, Secretary

P R O C E E D I N G S

turns.label: ACTING PRESIDENT DeFRANCISCO
turns.text:
The Senate will come to order. Would everyone please rise and repeat with me the Pledge of Allegiance.

The invocation today will be given by Imam Abdur Rahim Muhammad, the Chaplain and Islamic Services Coordinator of the Elmira Correctional Facility.

turns.label: IMAM ABDUR RAHIM MUHAMMAD
turns.text:
Dear members of the Senate and all those present, peace be upon you. Inshallah 'alaihim, salam alaihum!

Please allow me to express my gratitude to Senator Kuhl and those who have made this historic occasion possible. I thank Almighty God and am once honored and humbled to represent the Nation of Islam and the hundreds of thousands of Muslims everywhere across New York State. As probably the first and more probably not the last Muslim to open in prayer before this honorable gathering, let me make but one request, that each of us look to our own beliefs, values, disciplines and principles to find instead of that in which we could angrily disagree, those great many things on which, with united hearts and minds, we can and should act together to build a better reality for everyone under the blessings of the one God of us all.

I am blessed to be able to work with men in prison every day and just recently returned from Kazakhstan, a country where entire people was freed from mental and spiritual incarceration. In prayer, let us see the challenge of responding to freedom by respecting it.

Islam is a religion that has been represented and also misrepresented. In repre senting it here, I reflect on the words of Imam W. D. Muhammad who once said it's not who we are; it's what we represent that is important. This religion of peace is nowhere better repre sented than in the opening seven verses of the Qur'an, in which I pray that those honored lawmakers here will find its echo in their own minds and hearts with deeds, words and translation, we pray.

A'udhu billahi minash shaitanir rajim.

I seek refuge in the forces of Almighty God from all evil.

Bismillahir rahmanir rahim.

The merciful benefactor of the merciful redeemer.

Al hamdu lil lahi rabbil alamin.

Praise be to Allah, the cherisher and sustainer of the word.

Arrahmanir rahim.

The merciful benefactor, the merciful redeemer.

Maliki Yawmuddin.

Master of the day of judgment.

Iyyaka na'budu wa iyyaka nasta'in.

You do we worship and Your help do we seek.

Ihdinas siratal mustaqim. Show us the straight way.

Siratal ladhina 'amta 'alaihim, ghairil maghdubi 'alaihim wa lad dallin.

The way of those on whom You have bestowed Your grace, those whose portion is not ra, and who go not astray. Amin, amin. Amen.

turns.label: THE SECRETARY
turns.text:
Legislative Resolution, by Senator Kruger and others: Legislative Resolution proclaiming the month of September, 1995 as Menopause Awareness Month in the state of New York.

WHEREAS, menopause by the year 2000 will begin to affect 44 million American women, over 3 million in New York State.

It has already affected millions more according to the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists. The results will be a national health concern of dramatic proportions unless women are better educated about the changes of menopause and the measures that can prolong and enhance their lives.

If not properly treated by a trained physician, the health risk of perimenopausal and post-menopausal women can result in an increased number afflicted by osteoporosis or cardiovascular disease.

Estrogen depletion which occurs in menopause results in an increase in cardio vascular disease, resulting in over 530,000 deaths of women per year. These numbers could reach staggering proportions with the aging of the "baby boom" generation.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that this legislative body pause in its deliber ations and proclaim the month of September, 1995 as Menopause Awareness Month in the state of New York; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that a copy of this resolution, suitably engrossed, be transmitted to the American Menopause Foundation, a not-for-profit national support network of women, families, corporations and health care professionals committed to research, education, public awareness, for all women who need support and help.

turns.label: ACTING PRESIDENT DeFRANCISCO
turns.text: Senator Kruger.

turns.label: SENATOR KRUGER
turns.text:
Yes, Mr. President. I would like to now recognize with us today several individuals who have been responsible in not only preparing this resolution but bringing this issue to the fore front.

I would like to recognize the presence of Drs. Michael and Gerard Terrato, practicing obstetrics and gynecologists in Brooklyn, who have been my advisers in this particular resolution; additionally, we have with us today, Miss Barbara Pettit, representing the Beth Israel Medical Center and Miss Marie Longo, the president of a newly founded organization which has its headquarters in New York City and currently subscribes to a membership of over 20,000 members nationwide - individuals, women, who are afflicted with the scourge of the symptoms of menopause.

I thank them for their cooperation in making this issue an important one, and I look forward to working with them in the future.

Thank you, Mr. President.

turns.label: ACTING PRESIDENT DeFRANCISCO
turns.text:
Thank you, Senator. The resolution was previously adopted on March 14th.

turns.text:

turns.label: THE SECRETARY
turns.text: Those recorded in the negative on Calendar Number 528, are Senators Abate, Connor, Gold, Kruger, Montgomery, Paterson, Smith.

turns.label: ACTING PRESIDENT DeFRANCISCO
turns.text: Results.

turns.label: THE SECRETARY
turns.text: Ayes 42, nays 7.

turns.label: ACTING PRESIDENT DeFRANCISCO

turns.label: SENATOR BRUNO
turns.text: Mr. President, can we now return to Calendar Number 504. Senator Skelos is in the chamber.

turns.label: ACTING PRESIDENT DeFRANCISCO
turns.text: Secretary will read.

turns.label: THE SECRETARY
turns.text: Calendar Number 504, by Senator Skelos, Senate Print 1743-A, an act to amend the General Obligations Law, in relation to exoneration of certain crime victims.

turns.label: ACTING PRESIDENT DeFRANCISCO
turns.text: I believe Senator Paterson previously requested an explanation on this bill, Senator Skelos.

turns.label: SENATOR SKELOS
turns.text:
Mr. President, this bill amends the General Obligations Law by returning the assumption of risk doctrine to civil lawsuits. In an action for damages, if the defendant shows that the injury sustained by the plaintiff arose during the commission or attempted commission by the plaintiff of certain enumerated crimes and that the actions of the defendant were justified pursuant to Article 35 of the Penal Law, then the plaintiff is deemed to assume all the risk of injury coming from the encounter with the victim and that proof shall constitute a complete defense to the action.

The defendant must furnish proof by a preponderance of evidence by showing that the plaintiff committed the crime and that the defendant's actions were justified.

turns.label: ACTING PRESIDENT DeFRANCISCO
turns.text: Senator Paterson.

turns.label: SENATOR PATERSON
turns.text: Mr. President, would Senator Skelos yield for a question?

turns.label: SENATOR SKELOS
turns.text: Yes, I will.

turns.label: ACTING PRESIDENT DeFRANCISCO
turns.text: Senator Skelos, will you yield? He yields.

turns.label: SENATOR PATERSON
turns.text: Actually, Senator, I like this bill, and I want to vote for it. I just wanted to ask you if the whole difference between our criminal and our civil system is actually the standard of proof. Don't you think that sometimes the -- there could be an action that could be taken that certainly would not incur any criminal liability but, because of the different standard of proof being the preponderance of the evidence, would incur civil liability to the individual in this case who would be the victim of a crime, or a good samaritan or someone who is intervening?

turns.label: SENATOR SKELOS
turns.text: It's my belief that, with the enumerated crimes and the fact that the act had to be justified, that the answer would be no, and that's my opinion.

turns.label: SENATOR PATERSON
turns.text:
Thank you very much.

Mr. President, on -- on this bill.

I think we just have to be careful when we start, in a sense, creating a situation where there can be no action on the part of individuals. In this particular case we're talking about crime victims or we're talking about good samaritans who intervene in an actual crime.

There's certainly been a number of situations where people intervened, and they actually wound up being sued themselves. It's really very wrong when it happens. It's a kink in our criminal justice system, and I think it's very much satisfied by this particular bill. I just hope that we will be cautious in future legislation to make sure that we never lose sight of the fact that we still have a -- a civil system and that the standard of proof there is met not by proving beyond a reasonable doubt but by proving by preponderance of the evidence.

turns.label: ACTING PRESIDENT DeFRANCISCO
turns.text: Please read the last section.

turns.label: THE SECRETARY
turns.text: Section 2. This act shall take effect on the 1st day of November.

turns.label: ACTING PRESIDENT DeFRANCISCO
turns.text:
Call the roll.

(The Secretary called the roll. )

turns.label: THE SECRETARY
turns.text: Those recorded in the negative on Calendar Number 504 are Senators Connor and Gold. Ayes 48, nays 2.

turns.label: ACTING PRESIDENT DeFRANCISCO
turns.text:
The bill is passed.

Senator Skelos, that completes the reading of the controversial calendar.
